This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #22336: Very similar feature request (also by the same author) proposing more intelligent `edit` permission patterns, including absolute path support and worktree-boundary enforcement
- #20045: Bug report documenting the inconsistency between `edit` (relative paths) and `external_directory` (absolute paths) permission matching — the same root problem described here

On discord @justfortheloveof (discord handle) suggested that simply implementing proper globbing (as is also documented?) would do the trick as well. I wrote a new feature request for that and closing this one in favor of that one.

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #7407: Requests scoped permission overrides for skills and commands — nearly identical concept of allowing slash commands to temporarily restrict/override tool permissions during execution.

The globbing can simply happen against the relative path OR the absolute path as a function of whether or not the glob pattern looks like a relative path or an absolute path itself.

Currently all "edit" patterns look like relative paths, or they would never match anything.
There is no reason not to match patterns (added in the future) that look like absolute paths (aka, the pattern starts with '/' on linux, or 'C://' or whatever on Windows) against the absolute filepath.

On top of that I think we really should use proper globbing. Having a `*` match anything even `../` is unacceptable.

I closed #22336 in favor of this one although it has an orthogonal component that I think we should keep, namely that (glob) patterns that return true when passed to `path.isAbsolute` should be matched to the absolute filepath, otherwise to the relative filepath. And treat everything the same (read, edit, external_directory, list).  Doing that then also addresses #20045 completely.

> By doing so, the model no longer reasons, and within the context of code, it becomes significantly less intelligent.

Not exactly. Model still can reason if you toggle it in `ctrl + t`, the default one in with reasoning None.

As a daily user, I frequently need to share screenshots of bugs, terminal errors, and UI issues. Currently, I have to:

1. Describe the screenshot in text (often incomplete)
2. Upload it to a third-party service
3. Share the link

This workflow is cumbersome and error-prone. Image support would be a massive quality-of-life improvement.

Use cases that would greatly benefit:
- Sharing error messages or stack traces from terminal screenshots
- Sharing UI/UX bugs directly from the browser
- Sharing architecture diagrams or flowcharts
- Collaborating on design decisions with visual references

Many competitors (Cursor, Copilot, Claude Desktop) already support this natively. It's become an expected feature for any modern AI coding assistant.

Looking forward to seeing this implemented!

Confirming this and adding some supporting evidence on root cause.

**It's not the model and not Prettier — it's the XML serialisation layer.**

We hit this on a TypeScript codebase and investigated thoroughly. Here's what we found:

When the agent writes a `newString` containing TypeScript generics via the Edit tool, the `<T>` angle brackets are being interpreted as XML tags by the tool call serialiser and stripped before the content ever reaches the file system. The model outputs the correct content; the corruption happens in transit.

**Evidence:**
- OpenCode's session DB showed the agent writing `type AnyArray<T> = Array<T>` at one timestamp, and the subsequent `oldString` read-back showing `type AnyArray<T> = Array` on disk — the `<T>` on the right side was gone
- We ran the same source through Prettier 3.0.0 and 3.8.x with the project's actual `.prettierrc.json` — the generic survived byte-for-byte intact both times. Prettier is not involved.
- The loop behaviour (agent keeps trying to re-insert the generic but nothing sticks) is explained by the same mechanism: every write attempt strips `<T>` again

**The workaround in this thread is correct**: using bash/Python to write file content sidesteps the XML serialisation path. Claude's own compacted context in this thread correctly identified this: _"The Edit tool treats `<` as HTML"_.

The fix needs to be in how the Edit/Write tool parameters are serialised — `<` and `>` in `newString`/`content` values need to be escaped as `<`/`>` before XML wrapping, or the tool parameters need a different transport (e.g. base64 for content containing angle brackets).

I just spent a couple of hours trying to understand this issue (apparently I have nothing better to do) and want to share what I found, since others also seemed puzzled why https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/commit/6ecd011e51f8e38bdf1287e0d054e650437f95fc would constitute a solution for this issue. In particular, I don't quite understand why @dan-and [called it ](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/7101#issuecomment-3828733060) "a solution" [that is ](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/7101#issuecomment-3910335526) "fine for me", given that what he was looking for in the OP was a way of replacing the hard coded base prompts without recompiling the app after every change to a customized prompt. 

How could the introduction of the `OPENCODE_MODELS_PATH` environment variable help achieve that?

One possibility might have been that the shape of the `model-api.json` would allow us to pass a system prompt  as part of the models configuration file, but I could find no evidence that this is the case. As far as I can tell, it does not provide a direct way to supply custom prompt text. At most, it may indirectly affect which bundled prompt family is selected, because prompt selection is based on the model ID. But this is ony about switching around the existing system prompts, not replacing them with a custom prompt.

What seems more relevant is that replacing the system prompt has been possible already before https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/commit/6ecd011e51f8e38bdf1287e0d054e650437f95fc, namely via. `agent.<name>.prompt` in `opencode.json` (which then becomes `input.agent.prompt` internally):

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/6ecd011e51f8e38bdf1287e0d054e650437f95fc/packages/opencode/src/session/llm.ts#L65-L80

Contrary to [the assumtion](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/7101#issuecomment-3762253865) that 

> the Agent is on top of the system prompt 

this code above indicates that `input.agent.prompt` is indeed passed on *instead* of the provider prompt, which means - as [mentioned](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/7101#issuecomment-3762192334) by @malhashemi - that 

> You can in theory write your own custom prompt for the build agent if you would like to

So, unless I am misunderstanding something here, the possibility to overwrite the system prompt already existed before commit 6ecd011, but it was (and still is, I suppose) not clearly documented.

For sure, there would be much [more convenient ways](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/7264) of doing this, but the basic functionality seems to be there. If the goal is just to replace the base/provider prompt, patching/plugins may not be necessary, right?

Is that what everybody already understands and does? 

Or are you trying to control some of the other layers that get added on top of the base prompt? In that case, I can see why the current is not satisfactory.
